findings.summary: One bullet packs three separate flags (-F, -w, -o) into a single line.
findings.evidence: -F literal text, -w whole words, -o only the match
findings.fix: Split into three one-line bullets, or add -F, -w and -o to the flag table, with each code example next to its flag.

findings.summary: Bullets combine unrelated ideas, so a skimmer must parse two facts per line.
findings.evidence: uniq -c counts; uniq -d shows only duplicates
findings.fix: Move uniq -c and uniq -d into a small flag table or split them into separate bullets.

findings.summary: The common mistakes are a bare list of fragments with no reason or fix next to each.
findings.evidence:
Useless cat file | grep x: use grep x file
uniq without sort
Unquoted patterns
xargs rm without previewing
findings.fix: Turn it into a two-column table (Mistake | Fix or why), e.g. 'uniq without sort | only adjacent duplicates collapse'.

findings.summary: The flag table puts an example command inside the Effect column, which mixes explanation with code.
findings.evidence: -I{} | places the argument anywhere: xargs -I{} cp {} /backup
findings.fix: Keep the Effect cell to the one-line idea and put the cp example in the bash block.

findings.summary: Table rows contain a literal pipe character, which makes the columns ambiguous when skimming.
findings.evidence:
cmd | tee f | write file, pass on
Count | sort | uniq -c
findings.fix: Put the tee row in its own code line or note, and use a different layout (e.g. code-formatted cells) for rows whose commands contain pipes.

findings.summary: The recipes line is a prose list that names the recipes before the code, and the code block does not match it one-to-one.
findings.evidence: Top-N, safe delete (preview with echo), count matches
findings.fix: Replace the line with a comment above each command in the bash block, e.g. '# Top-N', '# preview delete', '# count matches'.
